svg.aria-label: An inner IP packet from Bob to the Pi's private address, wrapped in encrypted WireGuard inside UDP inside IP addressed to Grandpa's router
svg.text: The packet Bob’s laptop wants to send, to Grandpa’s Pi’s private address:

g.text: = 108 bytes: 20 IP + 8 UDP + 16 WireGuard header + 48 sealed + 16 tag
Grandpa’s router forwards UDP port 51820 to the Pi (Chapter 22). The Pi’s WireGuard checks the tag, unwraps
the packet, and hands it to its network stack as if it had arrived on a cable called wg0. The reply goes back the same way.

ol.li: Bob wants to reach the Pi as if he were at Grandpa’s house, on its private address. But private addresses can’t cross the internet (Chapter 22), and anyone could read the packet.

So his laptop wraps the whole packet up: encrypts it, and puts it inside an ordinary UDP datagram, addressed to Grandpa’s router, which the internet knows how to deliver. The sizes are from the lab’s real ping.
At the other end of the tunnel, the wrapping comes off. To the Pi, Bob’s laptop is just another computer on a network called wg0.

figure.figcaption: A tunnel: a packet inside a packet.
